title: refresh token replay after node restart leads to legacy session binding to new org context
creator: Arielle Chen
description:
Summary: Multiple Dedicated/Private customers have reported intermittent cross-org access where long-lived sessions rebind to the wrong org after a node restart. Customers observe that requests authenticated with an ostensibly rotated refresh token occasionally accept cached/stale session state and are evaluated against a different org scope. This surfaced as a P0 escalation from two customers in EU region on 2025-11-11.

Reproduction (observed):
- Customer rotates API keys / performs key roll (or nodes are restarted during maintenance).
- A small percentage of refresh flows return a refreshed access token but the evaluation pipeline uses a cached session descriptor (from before rotation) due to a replayed refresh event on node startup.
- Result: token presents valid, but org-scoping metadata bound to the session is from a previously handled tenant, causing authorization checks to allow access to resources outside the caller's org.

Investigation notes:
- Initial triage (2025-11-12): logs show replay of refresh requests received immediately after node bootstrap. The node-level session cache (LRU in-memory) is repopulated from local snapshot and an in-flight refresh queue is drained without verifying latest org mappings from central store.
- Correlation: customers affected were using Private deployments with edge autoscale and quick rolling restarts during key rotation windows.
- Root cause hypothesis: refresh request handling path assumes idempotent semantics but does not enforce a canonical validation step against authoritative apikey->org binding during the final acceptance path when the node's local cache was restored. Node restart plus race with key rotation allows an older binding to be reused.

Root cause (final):
- The refresh-token handler uses a two-step flow: (1) local session lookup / KV cache; (2) lock-free issuance of new access token. During node restart we replay queued refresh attempts using the restored cache state; the code path did not re-validate the apikey->org binding against the central tenant mapping service when the refresh token's sequence ID was lower than the last-seen on the new control plane. The missing authoritative rebind check allowed stale org-scoping metadata to be packaged into freshly minted tokens.

Interim mitigations applied (timeline):
- 2025-11-13: Emergency hotfix deployed to edge: reject post-restart refresh attempts that arrived within 30s of node bootstrap (fail closed). Deployed to affected Private clusters as configuration toggle. Slack: #inc-auth-ops thread linked below.
- 2025-11-14: Added short-circuit that forces authoritative org-lookup for any refresh requests during a 5-minute window after rotation events. Successfully reduced reproductions to zero for two customers (logs/metrics linked).

Proposed permanent fix:
1) Change refresh acceptance path to include authoritative apikey->org verification step (call tenant-metadata service with strong consistency read) before minting access token when a node has been restarted within the last N minutes or when refresh token TTL indicates potential race.
2) Harden node bootstrap: drain/replay queue only after cache tombstones are validated and a fresh binding snapshot is pulled.
3) Add a database-backed refresh-id monotonic guard per-apikey to reject refresh replays with sequence IDs <= last_accepted. This requires a lightweight write path on refresh acceptance (optimizable with a per-key compact tombstone).

Trade-offs discussed: 
- Latency: authoritative lookup adds ~8-15ms p99 on refresh flows. We measured network cost and decided to restrict authoritative check to two cases: node-restart windows and when token sequence is older than cached threshold. Full authoritative check on all refreshes was rejected due to tail-latency concerns and customer SLAs.
- Consistency vs throughput: adding a write for monotonic guard increases write ops per refresh but keeps checks local and robust. We considered Redis-based compare-and-set vs direct DB row update; chosen path is Redis CAS with fallback to DB for cold keys.

Fix plan and tasks: (owner tasks)
- Diego: implement authoritative verification hook + config flag to enable strict-mode (ENG-224512-1).
- Priya (infra): implement safe queue drain semantics in node-bootstrap (ENG-224512-2).
- Jordan (platform): add Redis monotonic guard pattern and migration plan for cold keys (ENG-224512-3).
- QA: write regression tests that simulate node restarts, key rotation, and replayed refreshes across dedicated/private clusters (ENG-224512-4).

Rollout and verification: 
- Canary: enable strict-mode on 5% of Private clusters for 48 hours, capture refresh fail rates, latency impacts, and any customer-visible errors.
- Full rollout: after 72h of green canary with no customer regressions, flip enforcement to 100% and retire 30s bootstrap reject hotfix.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for authoritative check code path.
- Integration test harness (k8s) to simulate rolling restarts + concurrent key rotation (script: tests/repro/refresh-replay.sh).
- E2E production-sim tests using staging data and chaos monkey to reproduce node restarts.

Monitoring and alerts:
- Add metric: refresh_replay_rejects_by_node_bootstrap and org_binding_mismatch_rate.
- Set alert: paging if org_binding_mismatch_rate > 0.1% over 5m in production cluster.

Links and artifacts: 
- Confluence incident writeup: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-224512+refresh-replay-incident
- GitHub PR (work in progress): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/14270
- Hotfix PR that temporarily rejects post-bootstrap refreshes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/14244
- Monitoring dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/refresh-replay/overview
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01AUTHOPS/p1699861234000210

Customer comms: 
- 2025-11-15: Sent interim mitigation notice to affected customers; SLA credit offered.
- 2025-11-20: Follow-up with detailed timeline and planned permanent fix.

Open questions / blockers: 
- Security review of Redis-based monotonic guard (Priya awaiting Sec team signoff).
- Confirmation of performance impact on Dedicated customers with high refresh throughput.

Next steps (this week):
- Merge authoritative check with feature flag behind runtime config (target: 2025-11-25).
- Start canary on 2025-11-27 for 48h.
- Post-canaray verification and finalize migration plan for monotonic guard (target completed: 2025-12-05).
reproduction_steps: Rotate API key or trigger node rolling restart on Private cluster
Initiate multiple concurrent refresh requests from a single client while node is restarting
Observe access tokens minted and verify org-scoping metadata against a different org
Check node bootstrap logs for replayed requests and cache restore events
impact: Intermittent cross-org data exposure for Private/Dedicated customers during node restart + key rotation windows; observed in production for two customers; high severity (P0).
root_cause: Missing authoritative apikey->org validation during refresh acceptance when node cache is restored after restart, allowing stale binding to be included in new tokens.
mitigation: Deployed temporary reject-on-bootstrap window and short-term authoritative lookup for refreshes; planning permanent fix with authoritative checks and monotonic refresh guards.
fix_plan: Implement authoritative verification hook + safe bootstrap replay + Redis monotonic guard; canary then full rollout. Detailed task owners assigned.
rollout_plan: Canary 5% private clusters 48h -> monitor -> 100% after green. Retire hotfix post-rollout.
test_plan: Unit, integration (simulated restart + rotation), E2E chaos tests. Regression tests added to CI.
notes: Prefer Redis CAS for performance with DB fallback to avoid high write amplification
Keep strict-mode behind runtime config for emergency rollback
Coordinate with Security + Compliance for private deployments before full rollout
